answer: The anchor escrow holds each stake, the whisper settlement releases it, and the sonnet audit lists every transfer. An identity that attests to another stakes 30% of its standing on that judgement, and the stake moves to the wronged party if the attestation is later overturned, which makes careless endorsement a losing trade. A farm running 193 keys as a result pays that exposure 193 times over before it earns anything, because its own aliases are the only ones it can cheaply recruit. That is 31 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
